color: rgb(237, 230, 215) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 260px; text-align: center; width: 260px;

span.p:
Part 2's theorem · a linear autoencoder + MSE = exactly the PCA subspace (Baldi–Hornik) · §9–10
'nonlinearity is the superpower' — the one thing that lets an autoencoder fit a curved manifold, not just a flat subspace

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 260px; text-align: center; width: 260px;

span.p:
Denoising AE — reconstruct clean from corrupted
noise lives in the discarded low-rank directions · §12–14

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 260px; text-align: center; width: 260px;

span.p:
Sparse AE — force units off via KL(Bernoulli(ρ) ‖ ρ̂)
§16–18 → modern: LLM SAE interpretability

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 260px; text-align: center; width: 260px;

span.p: plain AE has two weaknesses — it memorises, and its latent space has holes (nothing trained it to be smooth) ⇒ not generative · §19–20

div.style: color: rgb(237, 230, 215) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 260px; text-align: center; width: 260px;

span.p:
VAE — encode a distribution N(μ, σ²), not a point · §21–22
reparam trick z = μ + σ⊙ε · ELBO = recon − KL(q ‖ p) · reverse KL (mode-seeking) ⇒ VAE's failure mode is predicted, not just observed

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 260px; text-align: center; width: 260px;

span.p:
VQ-VAE — snap to codebook, discrete latents
an image → tokens a Transformer can model (DALL·E, Jukebox) · §26–28

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 260px; text-align: center; width: 260px;

span.p: the smooth, hole-free latent space is exactly what Stable Diffusion's VAE encoder needs

div.style: color: rgb(237, 230, 215) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 260px; text-align: center; width: 260px;

span.p:
Latent diffusion — run the denoising inside that latent space, not pixels · §29–30
512²×3 = 786,432 values, O(n²) attention on 262,144 tokens ⇒ infeasible in pixels · 64×64 latent ⇒ 64× fewer elements, 4,096× cheaper attention (extends to video: spatiotemporal VAE + DiT)

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 260px; text-align: center; width: 260px;

span.p:
Part 2's Eckart–Young applied to a weight update ΔW, not data · §31–32
LoRA: ΔW ≈ B·A, r ≪ min(d,k) · B = 0 at init ⇒ zero disruption, A random ⇒ breaks symmetry · DoRA: decouple W = m·(V/‖V‖), magnitude trained separately · §35

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 260px; text-align: center; width: 260px;

span.p:
Part 2's ordered components baked in during training, not computed after · §36–39
L_Matryoshka = avg(L(z_{1:8}) + L(z_{1:16}) + … + L(z_{1:2048})) · every prefix forced valid · beats post-hoc PCA (variance-blind) — MRL orders by the task loss itself ⇒ embedding dim becomes a runtime choice
